raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Replace the thread-based compile_regex_with_timeout() with a fork-based subprocess that is SIGKILL'd on deadline expiry. The previous ThreadPoolExecutor approach could not cancel already-running callables, allowing adversarial regex patterns to accumulate CPU/memory-consuming compiler workers after each timeout error.

- Use multiprocessing fork context for fast subprocess creation
- SIGKILL + join the child before returning ValueError on timeout
- Add global semaphore (VLLM_REGEX_COMPILATION_MAX_CONCURRENT, default 1) to bound concurrent compilation processes
- Adapt xgrammar/outlines/lm-format-enforcer call sites to use picklable top-level workers with serialize/deserialize round-trips
- Add regression tests asserting zero lingering processes after timeout

@jperezdealgaba, thank for your PR! I studied your patch and I see a fundamental problem that makes the whole idea of replacing threads to standalone processes using fork incompatible with current vLLM architecture.
The problem is that vLLM cannot create processes after cuda context was initialized, only spawn is allowed. This is intentionally policy, see for example [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/utils/system_utils.py#L148-L149).

If the problem still exists in your opinion but you simply have no time to resolve it yourself, please, create a separate bug report and link this attempt to it.

Thanks for the review. Sorry for the delay in answering, this one got missed in my inbox. I have redone the MR to try to match vLLM policy

Regex compilation now runs in a small pool of long-lived workers started through `get_mp_context()`, so the start method follows the existing policy (spawn once CUDA is initialized, and likewise for Ray, NUMA, and WSL). A compile that misses the deadline SIGKILLs that worker and the next job starts a replacement, so the timed-out work does not keep running. The concurrency cap is unchanged.

The timeout hole is still present on main, so I am keeping this pull request open with that design instead of the fork approach. The branch is rebased onto current main.

@jperezdealgaba, thank for your PR! I studied your patch and I see a fundamental problem that makes the whole idea of replacing threads to standalone processes using fork incompatible with current vLLM architecture.
The problem is that vLLM cannot create processes after cuda context was initialized, only spawn is allowed. This is intentionally policy, see for example [here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/utils/system_utils.py#L148-L149).

Thanks for the review. Sorry for the delay in answering, this one got missed in my inbox. I have redone the MR to try to match vLLM policy

Regex compilation now runs in a small pool of long-lived workers started through `get_mp_context()`, so the start method follows the existing policy (spawn once CUDA is initialized, and likewise for Ray, NUMA, and WSL). A compile that misses the deadline SIGKILLs that worker and the next job starts a replacement, so the timed-out work does not keep running. The concurrency cap is unchanged.

The timeout hole is still present on main, so I am keeping this pull request open with that design instead of the fork approach. The branch is rebased onto current main.
